title: A Rover in a Building: A Plan, a Range Sensor, a Map and a Supervisor, and What Happens When Somebody Steps Out

questions.question: The supervisor was on and the limiter off, and somebody stepped into the path. What happened?
options: The supervisor stopped the rover when the person appeared
The rover slowed to half speed
Nothing: the supervisor decides from what it is told, and with no limiter nothing told it about the person (144 ticks in contact)
The fence stopped the rover
questions.explanation: The supervisor acts on what its monitors tell it. With the limiter off, no monitor reported the person, so its cap stayed at the top speed.

questions.question: How long was the rover with neither the limiter nor the supervisor in contact with the person?
options: 144 ticks of 0.05 s, 7.2 seconds, pushing against them until they left
Not at all: it steered round them
1 tick, before it backed off
For the whole run
questions.explanation: It pressed against the person until they walked away and then drove on to the goal. A test that only checked arrival would have passed.

questions.question: Why did a rover that never forgets wait for 120 s at a doorway that had been clear since 20 s?
options: The planner had run out of iterations
The person came back at 20 s
The map marked the doorway as a wall for good
It was waiting out of sight of the doorway
questions.explanation: Nothing on the map could change: a belief nobody can check does not go away. From where it waited the doorway was out of view, so no beam could clear it. Forgetting after 4 s made it go and look, and it arrived 7 s after the person left.

questions.question: The link was lost at 5 s and came back at 9 s. Why did the rover stay stopped?
options: The planner had no path while the link was down
The range sensor failed at the same time
The battery monitor derated it to zero
The supervisor latches, and a reset is a person's decision: cause link, still at the end
questions.explanation: A stop for a lost link is latched. The link's return does not restart the rover; only a reset does, and nobody gave one.

questions.question: What is the difference between the limiter alone and the supervisor with it, when the sensor dies?
options: None: both stop and both record the cause
The limiter alone does not stop
Both stop, but the limiter alone does it with no cause on record and would restart when the sensor came back
The supervisor stops later, after 4.8 m
questions.explanation: The supervisor gives a cause, a latch and a reset. The limiter reads a NaN as a blocked path and sets the speed to zero. The supervisor adds what a person needs afterwards: why it stopped, and that it stays stopped.

questions.question: What should the README of a project like this show?
options: A video of the rover reaching the goal
The table of what each layer does, including the row where a layer on its own does nothing, and the rover waiting at a door that is open
Only the map of the building
The fastest run
questions.explanation: The rows where a layer alone did nothing, and where the rover sat at an open door, are the ones that show the system was really exercised.
